1950-a-woman-of-thirty.description: A book by Honore De Balzac. He seemed to take up the coquette’s part for her; perhaps of the two, he was the more gratified by the curious glances directed at those little feet, shod with plum-colored prunella; at the dainty figure outlined by a low-cut bodice, filled in with an embroidered chemisette, which only partially concealed the girlish throat.

arxiv-2011-04711.title: High | t | |t| diffractive vector meson production at the EIC
arxiv-2011-04711.creator: Michal Deák, Anna M. Staśto, Mark Strikman
arxiv-2011-04711.description: Abstract We investigate the prospects of the diffractive production of J / ψ J/\psi mesons at large momentum transfer | t | |t| at the future Electron Ion Collider in electron-proton collisions. In particular, we focus on the measurements of the rapidity gap size.

arxiv-2102-05520.title: A self-supervised, physics-aware, Bayesian neural network architecture for modelling galaxy emission-line kinematics 2021 A self-supervised, physics-aware, Bayesian neural network architecture for modelling galaxy emission-line kinematics – 4
arxiv-2102-05520.creator: James M. Dawson, Timothy A. Davis, Edward L. Gomez, Justus Schock
arxiv-2102-05520.description: Abstract In the upcoming decades large facilities, such as the SKA, will provide resolved observations of the kinematics of millions of galaxies. In order to assist in the timely exploitation of these vast datasets we explore the use of a self-supervised, physics aware neural network capable of Bayesian kinematic modelling of galaxies.

arxiv-2104-15044.title: Pulser: An open-source package for the design of pulse sequences in programmable neutral-atom arrays
arxiv-2104-15044.creator: Henrique Silvério, Sebastián Grijalva, Constantin Dalyac, Lucas Leclerc, Peter J. Karalekas, Nathan Shammah, Mourad Beji, Louis-Paul Henry, Loïc Henriet
arxiv-2104-15044.description: Abstract Programmable arrays of hundreds of Rydberg atoms have recently enabled the exploration of remarkable phenomena in many-body quantum physics. In addition, the development of high-fidelity quantum gates are making them promising architectures for the implementation of quantum circuits. We present here Pulser , an open-source Python library for programming neutral-atom devices at the pulse level.

arxiv-2110-06955.title: Deprojection of external barred galaxies from photometry 2021 Deprojection of external barred galaxies from photometry – 15
arxiv-2110-06955.creator: Behzad Tahmasebzadeh, ID Ling Zhu, ID Juntai Shen, ID Ortwin Gerhard, ID Yujing Qin ID
arxiv-2110-06955.description: Abstract The observations of external galaxies are projected to the 2D sky plane. Reconstructing the 3D intrinsic density distribution of a galaxy from the 2D image is challenging, especially for barred galaxies, but is a critical step for constructing galactic dynamical models.

arxiv-2205-05274.title: Connected power domination number of product graphs
arxiv-2205-05274.creator: S. Ganesamurthy, J. Jeyaranjani, R. Srimathi
arxiv-2205-05274.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the connected power domination number ( γ P , c \gamma_{P,c} ) of three standard graph products. The exact value for γ P , c ​ ( G ∘ H ) \gamma_{P,c}(G\circ H) is obtained for any two non-trivial graphs G G and H . H.

arxiv-2211-01732.title: Magnetism in Two-Dimensional Ilmenenes: Intrinsic Order and Strong Anisotropy
arxiv-2211-01732.creator: R.H Aguilera-del-Toro, M. Arruabarrena, A. Leonardo, A. Ayuela
arxiv-2211-01732.description: Abstract Iron ilmenene is a new two-dimensional material that has recently been exfoliated from the naturally-occurring iron titanate found in ilmenite ore, a material that is abundant on earth surface. In this work, we theoretically investigate the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of 2D transition-metal-based ilmenene-like titanates.

arxiv-2305-03215.title: Geodesically convex M M -estimation in metric spaces
arxiv-2305-03215.creator: Victor-Emmanuel Brunel
arxiv-2305-03215.description: Abstract We study the asymptotic properties of geodesically convex M M -estimation on non-linear spaces. Namely, we prove that under very minimal assumptions besides geodesic convexity of the cost function, one can obtain consistency and asymptotic normality, which are fundamental properties in statistical inference.

arxiv-2306-15808.title: Classification of Infant Sleep/Wake States: Cross-Attention among Large Scale Pretrained Transformer Networks using Audio, ECG, and IMU Data
arxiv-2306-15808.creator: \authorblockN Kai Chieh Chang \authorrefmark 1 \authorrefmark 2, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson \authorrefmark 1 \authorrefmark 2, Nancy L. McElwain \authorrefmark 2 \authorrefmark 4, Bashima Islam \authorrefmark 3 \authorblockA \authorrefmark 1 Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University o
arxiv-2306-15808.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by \authorblockN Kai Chieh Chang \authorrefmark 1 \authorrefmark 2, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson \authorrefmark 1 \authorrefmark 2, Nancy L. McElwain \authorrefmark 2 \authorrefmark 4, Bashima Islam \authorrefmark 3 \authorblockA \authorrefmark 1 Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University o. Infant sleep is critical to brain and behavioral development. Prior studies on infant sleep/wake classification have been largely limited to reliance on expensive and burdensome polysomnography (PSG) tests in the laboratory or wearable devices that collect single-modality data.

arxiv-2310-14882.title: On a Markov chain related to the individual lengths in the recursive construction of Kingman’s coalescent
arxiv-2310-14882.creator: Linglong Yuan
arxiv-2310-14882.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Linglong Yuan. Kingman’s coalescent is a widely used process to model sample genealogies in population genetics. Recently there have been studies on the inference of quantities related to the genealogy of additional individuals given a known sample. This paper explores the recursive (or sequential) construction which is a natural way of enlarging the sample size by adding individuals one after another to the sample genealogy via individual lineages to construct the Kingman’s coalescent.

arxiv-2406-03347.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
arxiv-2406-03347.creator: Mustafa Kalafat, Özgür Kelekçi, Mert Taşdemir
arxiv-2406-03347.description: Abstract In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

arxiv-2505-20979.title: MelodySim: Measuring Melody-aware Music Similarity for Plagiarism Detection
arxiv-2505-20979.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . We propose MelodySim , a melody-aware music similarity model and dataset for plagiarism detection. First, we introduce a novel method to construct a dataset with focus on melodic similarity. By augmenting Slakh2100; an existing MIDI dataset, we generate variations of each piece while preserving the melody through modifications such as note splitting, arpeggiation, minor track dropout (excluding bass), and re-instrumentation. A user study confirms that positive pairs indeed contain similar melodies, with other musical tracks significantly changed.

arxiv-2511-06961.title: Hybrid Autoencoders for Tabular Data: Leveraging Model-Based Augmentation in Low-Label Settings
arxiv-2511-06961.creator: Erel Naor, Ofir Lindenbaum
arxiv-2511-06961.description: Abstract Deep neural networks often underperform on tabular data due to sensitivity to irrelevant features and a spectral bias toward smooth, low-frequency functions, limiting their ability to capture sharp, high-frequency signals in low-label regimes. While self-supervised learning (SSL) holds promise in such settings, it remains challenging in tabular domains due to the limited availability of effective data augmentations.

arxiv-2604-22913.creator: Alexander J. Dittmann, Matteo Cantiello

britannica-1911-rondo.title: Rondo (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rondo.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rondo.description: Article 'Rondo' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. in verse; as may be seen, long before the development of instrumental forms, in some of the chansons of Orlando di Lasso. The rondeau en couplets of Couperin and his contemporaries shows both in name and form the same connexion with verse. It consists of the alternation between a single neatly rounded phrase and several slightly contrasted episodes (the couplets) without any important change of key.

pmc-10522404.title: Prevalence and Radiographic Features of Head and Neck Soft Tissue Calcifications on Digital Panoramic Radiographs: A Retrospective Study
pmc-10522404.creator: Aydan Acikgoz, Ozlem Akkemik
pmc-10522404.description: BackgroundIn this study, we aimed to determine the prevalence and radiographic features of incidental head and neck soft tissue calcifications (STCs) on panoramic imagesand assess their clinical significance.MethodologyFollowing well-established training and calibration procedures, 9,553 digital panoramic radiographs (DPRs) taken between January 1, 2021, and January 31, 22, were retrospectively evaluated. Only obvious calcifications and clear differential diagnoses were considered.

pmc-10525522.title: Does Decreased Vitamin D Level Trigger Bipolar Manic Attacks?
pmc-10525522.creator: Okan İmre, Mustafa Karaağaç, Cuneyt Caglayan
pmc-10525522.description: Background: Bipolar disorder is a chronic psychiatric disorder with depression and manic episodes. It is one of the leading causes of disease-related disability worldwide. Despite the presence of various alternative drug options for bipolar disorder, some patients do not adequately benefit from the treatment. Therefore, possible underlying mechanisms need to be clarified.

pmc-10558203.title: Diminishing neuronal acidification by channelrhodopsins with low proton conduction
pmc-10558203.creator: Rebecca Frank Hayward, F Phil Brooks, Shang Yang, Shiqiang Gao, Adam E Cohen, Jon T Sack, Rebecca Frank Hayward, F Phil Brooks, Shang Yang, Shiqiang Gao, Adam E Cohen
pmc-10558203.description: Many channelrhodopsins are permeable to protons. We found that in neurons, activation of a high-current channelrhodopsin, CheRiff, led to significant acidification, with faster acidification in the dendrites than in the soma. Experiments with patterned optogenetic stimulation in monolayers of HEK cells established that the acidification was due to proton transport through the opsin, rather than through other voltage-dependent channels.

pmc-11504658.title: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models in Chinese Medical Named Entity Recognition
pmc-11504658.creator: Zhichao Zhu, Qing Zhao, Jianjiang Li, Yanhu Ge, Xingjian Ding, Tao Gu, Jingchen Zou, Sirui Lv, Sheng Wang, Ji-Jiang Yang, Elpiniki I Papageorgiou, Pietro Aricò
pmc-11504658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has provided robust support for application tasks across various domains, such as name entity recognition (NER) in the general domain. However, due to the particularity of the medical domain, the research on understanding and improving the effectiveness of LLMs on biomedical named entity recognition (BNER) tasks remains relatively limited, especially in the context of Chinese text.

pmc-11522881.title: Strategic housing decisions and the evolution of urban settlements: optimality modelling and empirical application in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
pmc-11522881.creator: Natalia Fedorova, Anne Kandler, Richard McElreath
pmc-11522881.description: Investments in housing influence migration and landscape construction, making them a key component of human–environment interactions. However, the strategic decision-making that builds residential landscapes is an underdeveloped area of research in evolutionary approaches to human behaviour. Our contribution to this literature is a theoretical model and an empirical test of this model using data from Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

pmc-11561574.title: Complex left atrial appendage closure using 3D printing system simulation in a patient with mitral prosthetic valve: a case report
pmc-11561574.creator: Luca Vicini Scajola, Antonio Sanzo, Giulia Magrini, Stefania Marconi, Roberto Rordorf, Sarnadeep Kaur Marwaha, Georgios Benetos, Emmanouil Mantzouranis
pmc-11561574.description: BackgroundLeft atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAc) has emerged as a safe and effective alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and contraindications to OAC.Case summaryA 61-year-old woman with permanent AF and a history of mitral surgery replacement with mechanical prosthesis was referred to our cardiology department to undergo LAAc.

pmc-11579085.title: An easy and sensitive assay for acetohydroxyacid synthases based on the simultaneous detection of substrates and products in a single step
pmc-11579085.creator: Annika Engelhardt, Marco Ebeling, Elisabeth Kaltenegger, Dorothee Langel, Dietrich Ober
pmc-11579085.description: Acetohydroxyacid synthase (AHAS, EC 2.2.1.6) catalyzes the first step in the synthesis of the branched-chain amino acids valine, leucine, and isoleucine, pathways being present in plants and microorganisms, but not in animals. Thus, AHAS is an important target for numerous herbicides and, more recently, for the development of antimicrobial agents.

pmc-11678191.title: Evaluation of Recycled and Reused Metal Powders for DMLS 3D Printing †
pmc-11678191.creator: Simona Svozilova, Ivana Zetková, Juan Felipe Santa Marin, Jesús Arturo Torres Garay, Pan Gong
pmc-11678191.description: Metal powders for additive manufacturing are expensive, and producing new ones from mined metals has a negative ecological impact. In this work, recycled and reused metal powders from MS1 steel for direct metal laser sintering (DMLS) 3D printing were evaluated in the laboratory. The powders were recycled by melting followed by gas atomizing.

pmc-11814155.title: Effect of potato glycoside alkaloids on mitochondria energy metabolism of Fusarium solani, the root rot pathogen of Lycium barbarum
pmc-11814155.creator: Ruiyun Li, Bin Wang, Wei Chen, Chongqing Zhang, Nan Li, Yupeng Wang, Yuke Yan, Yuyan Sun, Jing He
pmc-11814155.description: Fusarium solani is a widely distributed pathogenic fungus that can cause soil borne diseases in various plants and is also one of the main pathogenic bacteria of Lycium barbarum root rot. This study employed tandem mass labeling (TMT) quantitative proteomics technology to investigate the antifungal mechanism of potato glycoside alkaloids (PGA) against Fusarium solani.

pmc-12365126.title: Associations of adolescent menstrual symptoms with school absences and educational attainment: analysis of a prospective cohort study
pmc-12365126.creator: Gemma Sawyer, Abigail Fraser, Deborah A. Lawlor, Gemma C. Sharp, Laura D. Howe
pmc-12365126.description: Menstrual symptoms may negatively impact academic achievement, but rigorous population-based studies are lacking. 2,698 participants from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC) self-reported heavy or prolonged bleeding and menstrual pain during adolescence and multivariable regression were used to estimate associations with linked data on absences and attainment at age 15/16, adjusting for confounders.

pmc-12366570.title: Application of machine learning in early childhood development research: a scoping review
pmc-12366570.creator: Faith Neema Benson, Daisy Chelangat, Willie Brink, Patrick N Mwangala, Akbar K Waljee, Cheryl A Moyer, Amina Abubakar
pmc-12366570.description: AbstractBackgroundEarly childhood development (ECD) lays the foundation for lifelong health, academic success and social well-being, yet over 250 million children in low- and middle-income countries are at risk of not reaching their developmental potential. Traditional measures fail to fully capture the risks associated with a child’s development outcomes.

pmc-12568264.title: Cellular eEF1G Inhibits Porcine Deltacoronavirus Replication by Binding Nsp12 and Disrupting Its Interaction with Viral Genomic RNA
pmc-12568264.creator: Weijia Yin, Xinna Ge, Lei Zhou, Xin Guo, Jun Han, Yongning Zhang, Hanchun Yang
pmc-12568264.description: Porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV) is an emerging pathogen that causes severe, often fatal, diarrhea in suckling piglets and has zoonotic potential. Its nonstructural protein 12 (Nsp12), functioning as the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), is a central component of the viral replication–transcription complex and a critical target for host antiviral mechanisms.

pmc-13083698.title: Predictive value of interim ¹¹C-choline PET/CT for response to radium-223 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
pmc-13083698.creator: Eman E. Ahmed, Jack R. Andrews, Mohamed E. Ahmed, Rimki Haloi, Lauren A. Rhodes, Mindie Mahon, Day A. Carter, Nancy Wei, Mattew P. Thorpe, Geoffrey B. Johnson, Eugene D. Kwon, Ayse Tuba Kendi
pmc-13083698.description: BackgroundRadium-223 (Ra-223) has been approved for the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with predominant osseous metastases. PSA flare phenomenon with Ra-223 limits its use as a prognostic tool to predict treatment response. Currently, there is a lack of diagnostic tools to predict treatment response to Ra-223.

pmc-13523493.title: Pitfalls encountered while projecting the future Israeli anesthesiologist workforce: lessons from the Israel anesthesiologist workforce study
pmc-13523493.creator: Ariel Wimpfheimer, Yehuda Ginosar, Daniela Quesada, Shai Fein, Charles Weissman, The Israel Anesthesiology Workforce Study Group
pmc-13523493.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe smooth and efficient operation of a country’s healthcare system is highly dependent on the size and specialty composition of its physician workforce. Therefore, it is incumbent upon a country’s healthcare leadership to continually examine the workforce situation in each medical specialty, especially critical specialties like anesthesiology, so as to detect issues that could lead to shortfalls and surpluses and then apply effective corrective actions.

pmc-13528027.title: Outcomes of total joint arthroplasty in patients with a history of native hip or knee septic arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13528027.creator: Chang-Rack Lee, Dae-Hyun Park, Yong-Uk Kwon, Ji-Hun Park, Dong-Yun Lee
pmc-13528027.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhether a history of native hip or knee septic arthritis is associated with an increased risk of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), aseptic revision, or reoperation after total joint arthroplasty (TJA) remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether patients with a history of native hip or knee septic arthritis (septic arthritis group) are at higher risk of PJI, aseptic revision, and reoperation after primary TJA than those without (nonseptic arthritis group).

pmc-13614832.title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases
pmc-13614832.creator: Jiayu Yan, Minyue Cao, Yan Ding, Yiqin Zhang, Yihan Sun, Genyi Jiang, Yanli Zhang, Luyao Kang, Xue Zhou, Jing Luo, Bilan Li
pmc-13614832.description: BackgroundObesity is a major global public health concern closely linked to the development and progression of various gynaecological disorders, particularly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometrial cancer. Incretins, a group of gut‐derived hormones primarily including glucagon‐like peptide‐1 (GLP‐1) and glucose‐dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), are widely recognised for their roles in glycemic control and insulin secretion.

pmc-13674320.title: Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers Measured by Capillary Blood Collection Versus Venous Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid
pmc-13674320.creator: Sara Ho, Ziling Shen, Alexandria Lewis, Megha Patel, Anny Zheng, Gianna Proscino, Thaovy Ho, Jiangxia Wang, Marilyn Albert, Abhay Moghekar
pmc-13674320.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveBlood biomarkers are increasingly critical for non‐invasive Alzheimer's Disease (AD) diagnostics and research but typically require on‐site processing. Remote point‐of‐care collection methods could enhance biomarker testing in clinical and research settings.
